fatal_errors: The proposed boron addition does not reconstruct the supported 4.2 at.% Cr intervention.
No evidence is provided that boron lowers the alloy density while preserving room-temperature and approximately 1000 °C mechanical properties.
The cited study concerns AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and does not support boron modification of HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed boron-rich phase and its strengthening or toughening role are unspecified and unsupported.
The experiment lacks quantitative rejection thresholds and does not specify loading mode, boron concentration, phase morphology, or high-temperature testing protocol.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the general density-versus-mechanical-performance objective and names the correct baseline alloy, but otherwise provides a speculative alternative. It misses the target intervention of Cr addition and the associated low-volume-fraction reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase, lattice contraction, solid-solution hardening, and crack-deflection/plasticity-compensation mechanism. It also gives no quantitative predictions comparable to the reported increases in yield strength and fracture strain. Merely specifying room temperature to 1000 °C is not an adequate boundary because the loading mode, exposure duration, microstructural stability, and acceptable property-retention criteria are absent. The proposed comparison could be a preliminary screen, but without explicit rejection criteria it is weakly falsifiable. The sole citation is materially irrelevant, so the boron hypothesis remains unsupported rather than a well-founded plausible alternative.
